newsitem.title: UK: British authorities discuss monetary policy.
newsitem.headline: British authorities discuss monetary policy.

text.p: Britain's finance minister, Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, met Bank of England Governor Eddie George Wednesday for their monthly meeting on monetary policy, but they made no announcement on interest rates.
Because their meeting began after the central bank had concluded its daily money market operations, any decision on interest rates was unlikely to be announced until Thursday morning.
The bank, which advises Clarke on monetary policy, has called publicly for official rates to be increased from the present 6.0 percent to prevent inflation taking off again.

But economists expected Clarke to leave rates unchanged this month, citing an unexpected drop in December manufacturing output and an apparent slowdown in consumer spending as evidence that there was no risk of the economy overheating.
